fixes.explanation: Yes! "The king had them cast in clay molds in the plain of the Jordan between Succoth and Zarethan." (1 Kings 7:46). That's a lot of molten bronze being poured out on that plain. I get nervous with a hot cookie sheet, so I tip my hat to them.

That's it! "Solomon left all these articles unweighed, because there were so many. The weight of the bronze could not be determined." (1 Kings 7:47). So many pieces that the weighing never happened. I can't even leave a cookie box unweighed without peeking, so that's a lot of bronze.

Joppa is a real place, but it's not where Huram comes from. The text says "Now King Solomon sent to bring Huram from Tyre." (1 Kings 7:13). Solomon is Israel's king, and he sent for his craftsman. Tyre, friend!

Stone shows up in this chapter, since the palace has big, costly stones (1 Kings 7:10). But the text describes Huram's skill in bronze. It says he had skill for "…every kind of bronze work." (1 Kings 7:14). So the answer is bronze, friend.

False is right! Huram "…came to King Solomon and carried out all his work." (1 Kings 7:14). Then "…Huram finished all the work that he had undertaken for King Solomon in the house of the LORD…" (1 Kings 7:40). He finished what he started. That's the kind of worker every boss prays for.

Right! Solomon "…brought in the items his father David had dedicated—the silver, the gold, and the furnishings…" (1 Kings 7:51). David, Israel's former king, set those things apart, and Solomon, his son, carried them in. So David's gifts ended up in the house of the LORD.

The priests are a fair guess, but that's not what this verse says. Solomon "…brought in the items his father David had dedicated—the silver, the gold, and the furnishings…" (1 Kings 7:51). So it was David, Solomon's father, who dedicated them. The verse doesn't mention the priests here.
Treasuries! Solomon "…placed them in the treasuries of the house of the LORD." (1 Kings 7:51). That's where David's silver, gold and furnishings went. Good work, baker!
